## P1: Self-Repair: Repairing Code with LLMs (Olausson et al., 2023) [arXiv:2306.09896]

**Core claim:** LLMs can self-repair code given execution feedback, but gains are modest (+0-10% pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP) unless feedback signal is rich.

**Methodology:** Generate initial solution → run tests → inject error trace back into prompt → regenerate. Up to 3 repair attempts. GPT-4 backbone. HumanEval + MBPP evaluation.

**Key findings:**
- Execution feedback alone gives small pass@1 gains (weaker than expected)
- GPT-4 benefits more from feedback than GPT-3.5 (model capability matters)
- Verbosity of feedback matters: error trace > pass/fail only
- Repair without feedback (just "fix this") barely helps

**Relevance to Gap 2:** Establishes execution monitoring as one feedback category baseline. Does NOT include static analysis or SMT — single-category study, no overhead measurement.

---

## P2: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement (Shinn et al., 2023) [arXiv:2303.11366]

**Core claim:** Verbal reinforcement (natural language reflection on failures) improves performance on sequential decision tasks including HumanEval coding.

**Methodology:** Agent reflects verbally on failure → appends to episodic memory → re-attempts. HumanEval pass@1 used as benchmark. GPT-4 backbone.

**Key findings:**
- HumanEval pass@1 improved from ~80% to ~91% with Reflexion on GPT-4
- Verbal reflection captures semantic failure mode better than raw error trace
- Memory budget limits practical depth of reflection chain

**Relevance to Gap 2:** Verbal/execution feedback category. No formal methods (no static analysis, no SMT). No overhead normalization. Single category, different feedback formulation than formal methods.

---

## P3: CodeT: Code Generation with Generated Tests (Bei Chen et al., 2022) [arXiv:2207.10397]

**Core claim:** Using LLM-generated test cases as execution oracle improves code selection and pass@k on HumanEval.

**Methodology:** Generate N code solutions + M test cases → cross-execute → select code-test cluster with highest agreement. CodeX backbone. HumanEval evaluation.

**Key findings:**
- pass@1 HumanEval improves substantially via test-based filtering (not repair — selection)
- Generated tests may share LLM biases but still improve over no filtering
- Complementary to repair-based approaches

**Relevance to Gap 2:** Execution oracle variant — different from repair loop. Confirms execution-based approaches are well-studied. No formal methods, no overhead comparison.

---

## P4: Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured NLP (Geng et al., 2023) [arXiv:2305.13971]

**Core claim:** CFG-constrained decoding guarantees syntactic correctness of LLM outputs for structured domains.

**Methodology:** Constrain beam search/sampling to valid grammar productions. Evaluated on semantic parsing and code generation tasks.

**Key findings:**
- Syntactic correctness guaranteed (0 parse errors)
- Semantic correctness improves modestly (syntactically valid ≠ semantically correct)
- Overhead: ~20-40% slowdown vs. unconstrained decoding

**Relevance to Gap 2:** Type/grammar checking category example. Shows one formal category with overhead characterization. Not applied to HumanEval/MBPP repair loop — only generation-time constraint, not post-generation repair. Different paradigm.
